definition: Costume archaeology: by analyzing the materials, forms, and patterns of clothing, ancient social hierarchy and cultural change are reconstructed.
core_case: Wukong's progression from 'tiger-skin skirt' to 'monk's robe' to 'Buddha's robe' reflects not only his inner journey but also the Ming Dynasty dress system.

costume_evolution.costume: Tongbi gibbon's gift · yellow short jacket
costume_evolution.ming_dynasty_parallel: Commoner clothing · yellow was a lowly color

character_costumes.evolution_pattern: U-shaped curve: nude → coarse cloth → gold armor → tiger skin → monk's robe → Buddha's robe · peak → trough → pinnacle
character_costumes.social_meaning: From king to disciple to Buddha, the costume mirrors the rise and fall of status.

character_costumes.social_meaning: From abandoned infant to Buddha, the costume mirrors a rise against the odds.

character_costumes.evolution_pattern: Down-then-up curve: marshal → pig → son-in-law → monk → envoy · great fall and rise
character_costumes.social_meaning: From marshal to pig to envoy, the costume mirrors status upheaval.

character_costumes.evolution_pattern: Down-then-up curve: general → demon → monk → arhat · upheaval
character_costumes.social_meaning: From general to demon to arhat, the costume mirrors status upheaval.

costume_insights: Wukong's costume evolution is the most complex, with 6 stages, reflecting the protagonist's inner journey.
All 4 protagonists' costume evolution follows the common pattern 'Heaven → mortal world → Buddhist fruit'.
Costume material strictly corresponds to status: gold = Buddha/king · coarse cloth = monk/commoner · nude = demon/beast.
Ming Dynasty dress system refracted: yellow was a lowly color (commoner) · gold-woven was noble (emperor) · kasaya marked monks.
At Buddhahood all 4 characters' costume materials unify into gold thread, reflecting the Buddhist ideal of 'equality of all beings'.
Costume evolution reflects Ming Dynasty social mobility: king ↔ disciple ↔ Buddha · status could convert.

ming_dynasty_parallel.imperial_robess: Imperial dragon robe: gold-woven + twelve emblem patterns (corresponds to Buddhahood)
ming_dynasty_parallel.monk_robes: Eminent monk's vestment: brocade kasaya + nine-ring staff (corresponds to Tang Sanzang's pilgrimage)
ming_dynasty_parallel.military_uniforms: General's armor: gold armor + war boots (corresponds to the Great Sage period)
ming_dynasty_parallel.commoner_clothing: Commoner clothing: coarse cloth short jacket + patched robe (corresponds to early pilgrimage)
ming_dynasty_parallel.official_uniforms: Official court robe: color-coded by rank (corresponds to the Altar Cleanser's robe)
